meta.title: Our Story — Meet the Team Teaching Armenian
meta.description: The story behind Haylingua — why we built it, our milestones, and the two-person team teaching Armenian to the diaspora with real audio and a modern, gamified curriculum.

hero.subtitle: A language spoken by millions across a worldwide diaspora, with almost nowhere good to learn it. This is why — and how — we're changing that.

story.heading: It started as a school assignment
story.paragraph1: In October 2024, Armen's IB teacher — Lilit Hakobyan, who has taught Armenian across the IB Diploma Programme and several other institutions — set him a project: build something that could actually teach Armenian to the diaspora, to the people growing up without easy access to the language of their grandparents. A month later, the first version of Haylingua existed.
story.paragraph2: That prototype sat for over a year while Armen finished the rest of the IB Diploma. In January 2026, with the idea still nagging at him, he started rebuilding Haylingua from scratch — a real backend, a real curriculum, real lesson content — with Lilit shaping how the app actually teaches the language. Haylingua is set to launch publicly in August 2026.

values.heading: Why we do it this way

cards.title: Armenian deserves better tools
cards.text: Most language apps treat Armenian as an afterthought, if they teach it at all. We built Haylingua because a language spoken by millions across a global diaspora deserves the same care as any of the world's biggest languages.

cards.title: Heritage, not just vocabulary
cards.text: For a lot of our learners, this isn't a new hobby — it's reconnecting with a grandparent, a hometown, a part of themselves. We design every lesson with that weight in mind.

cards.title: Built to actually stick
cards.text: Streaks, hearts, instant feedback, mistake review — the same habit-forming mechanics that make other language apps work, tuned specifically for how Armenian sounds and reads.

cards.title: A community, not just an app
cards.text: Friends, leaderboards, and a growing group of learners going through the exact same alphabet-to-conversation journey together.

cards.title: The mission comes first
cards.text: We started this because Armenian deserved better tools — every decision gets weighed against that, not against a roadmap.

cards.title: Ship small, ship often
cards.text: Two people building fast beats a big team building slowly. If you like moving quick and owning what you build end to end, you'll feel at home.

cards.title: Craft over speed-running
cards.text: We'd rather ship one lesson type that feels right than five that feel generic. Care shows, especially to a diaspora audience that's used to being an afterthought.

cards.title: It's personal for us
cards.text: This isn't a market-sizing exercise. Grandparents, hometowns, a language slipping away a generation at a time — that's who we're building for.

cards.title: Real backend, real curriculum
cards.text: FastAPI + Postgres backend, React frontend, a CMS we built ourselves to author every lesson, exercise, and achievement in the app.

cards.title: Every exercise is hand-built
cards.text: No AI-generated filler — Lilit designs how each concept is taught, Armen builds the exercise types to teach it well.

cards.title: Weekly, sometimes daily, ships
cards.text: New lesson content, features, and fixes go out constantly. You'll see your work live within days, not quarters.

cards.title: Just the two of us, for now
cards.text: A developer and a language teacher. Small enough that your work is never lost in a queue — you'll talk directly to whoever built the thing you're touching.
